newsitem.title: USA: Lead, zinc price to rise in '97 - industry officials.
newsitem.headline: Lead, zinc price to rise in '97 - industry officials.

text.p: The average LME price for lead is expected to reach 38 cents per pound in 1997, while the LME average zinc should rise to 52 cents per pound next year, industry officials said.
Thomas Parker, lead commodities purchasing manager at Exide Corp, said LME's average lead price should rise one cent next year over the 1996 forecast price of 37 cents per pound.
"I believe demand is going to continue to exceed supply," he said, speaking to industry executives at the Institute of Scrap Recyling Industries meeting in Chicago.
Meanwhile, LME zinc prices were forecast to rise by 15 percent in 1997.

Ed Schmidt, vice president of marketing and sales at Big River Zinc Corp, told executives at the conference that the LME price for zinc will average of $1,150 per tonne in 1997, or 52 cents per pound.
"We believe consumption will continue to grow in 1997, and that the big stockpile will be down to levels where the price starts going up," Schmidt said.
Big River Zinc Corp is a U.S.-based sudsidiary of Korea Zinc Co.
